approvalScope: Exact nine-source production/source-regression candidate only. Swift SDK/typecheck, controlled TLS and real service execution remain unperformed.
reviewedBehavior: Existing sealed Vault identity pins the original main/widget/share identifiers, team and ordered App Groups. Registration uses the existing account/session/transport only; no rename, wildcard, group stripping, deletion or certificate revocation route was added. API request/response leaves, APG3427HIY and enabled-feature preservation were read against the pinned AltSign implementation and SideStore source.

Raw Apple capability table has App groups yes under ADP, ADEP and the free Apple Developer column. This supports investigating the original group, not actual current-account server acceptance. No account request was made.

Fresh registration requests carry the existing team and immutable namespace/generation; after the fresh-anisette suspension the same request dispatcher rechecks epoch, credentials, Vault generation and optional live paired observation before transport dispatch. Old account validation/certificate/profile requests retain their existing checks, not an invented global new dispatch policy.

Only the live strict-mTLS Lockdown peer supplies UniqueDeviceID. Private construction, endpoint/peer-certificate/configuration binding, the real bounded monotonic socket deadline, cancellation wake and session ending delimit its use. It is not same-physical-device, no-VPN, installation-service or Apple authority evidence.

Existing pending certificate intent refuses a new refresh before registration; explicit reconciliation retains its original exact CSR/list association and never issues another CSR. For a lost registration ACK there is no automatic write retry; a later explicit operation relists and reuses an exact returned identity. This is not a durable exactly-once or complete-list attestation.

Partial registration dispatch and accepted ACK kinds are kept in EnrollmentFailure. Verified Vault publication remains the sole commit: registration ACK alone does not publish or establish rollback. StopSession failure preserves both original operation failure and cleanup failure, or the actual already-completed Lease. App/automatic callers preserve primary cancellation and error classification.

For configured paired targets, all three verified ModernProfile inner-DER ProvisionedDevices arrays must contain the exact UTF8 identifier before changing published manifest state. New issue, pending reconciliation and certificate-reuse profile renewal reach that same check. Default nil preserves account-only behavior and makes no target-device claim.

Source tests use existing real URLSession/URLProtocol, generated signed CMS/keychain Vault and actual TLS fixture owners. Four new noargument Test definitions cover original portal scope/re-list reuse, refusal/unknown ACK/held cancellation/stale generation and signed device-list negatives, actual App owner paired registration/cancellation, and typed GetValue observation ending. Their presence is authored coverage, not runtime passing evidence.

closedFindings.problem: The new cleanup wrapper originally bypassed the existing Owner classifier, hiding cancellation/storage/session primary errors behind operationFailed.
closedFindings.resolution: Owner unwraps RegistrationCleanupFailure and nested account publication failure; completed-Lease finalization classifies its StopSession error. Automatic Session error helpers also unwrap cleanup/enrollment. The existing new App method includes real TLS plus held remote mutation cancellation and Owner.problem==cancelled.

limits: No Swift grammar/parser, Apple SDK compilation, App test, TLS fixture, URLProtocol test, real device or Apple-account operation was run by author or reviewer for this candidate. Obvious source API/caller consistency was reviewed without claiming typechecking.

Unknown remote ACK and accepted registration facts are not atomic rollback or durable remote transaction proof. Stale or absent server lists can still lead an explicit retry to a typed duplicate/conflict response; the candidate does not silently rename or fall back.

The device-list match authenticates signed profile contents against an observed paired peer identifier. Existing code/profile anchor trust and actual Apple permission are distinct; all authority, replacement and complete-renewal flags remain false.

Current hardware route/VPN/entitlement/service/installation permission, actual replacement/launch/user-data preservation and unattended renewal require later controlled execution or device evidence. No new pairing import, store, network owner or protocol fallback was introduced.
